summary: The milestone completed 3 synthesis-only experiments in 0.0 total minutes, with 0 compute-bound experiments. The idle GPU snapshot is therefore not a compute-task utilization fault, and no parallel multi-model DualGPURunner requirement applies.
bottlenecks_identified: No execution bottleneck was measurable because all 3 experiments were synthesis-only and the supplied timing resolution reported 0 minutes per experiment.
Timing observability depended on disk-mtime reconstruction after the live git-log path found no milestone commits, so no phase-level duration cause was available.
improvements_suggested: Emit task-linked monotonic phase timestamps and a durable timing receipt during each experiment so milestone analysis does not depend on disk-mtime reconstruction.
Include compute classification, concurrent model count, and runner selection in each timing receipt so GPU utilization and DualGPURunner eligibility are auditable.
Include stable experiment IDs and acceptance counts in the milestone-scoped timing export so operational documentation does not require unavailable-data placeholders.
Keep synthesis-only work off the GPU dispatch path and reserve GPU scheduling for explicitly compute-bound work.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Write live task-linked phase and duration receipts for every experiment.
Record compute classification, model concurrency, GPU activity, and runner selection in one dispatch receipt.
Export stable experiment IDs and acceptance counts with the milestone timing data.
meta_reflection: The evidence supports a narrow conclusion: execution showed no measurable delay, while coarse fallback timing limited causal analysis. The savings estimate remains conservative because no measured counterfactual was supplied.
